source_title: Suikoden I&II HD Remaster Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars
continuity_scope: Konami's English-language Suikoden I HD Remaster Gate Rune War witness within Suikoden I&II HD Remaster Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars. Character evidence is restricted to the official Asia-English Suikoden I page's story/prologue and its 17 published character cards; a Konami Europe launch announcement confirms the 6 March 2025 global HD collection release and describes it as preserving the original story while updating presentation/systems. Suikoden II, original releases, translations, later games, adaptations, and any post-launch revisions are separate continuities/witnesses.
work_or_witnesses: Konami, About SUIKODEN I, Suikoden I&II HD Remaster official Asia-English website
Konami, Suikoden I&II HD Remaster Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars releases today, 6 March 2025
Konami, Basic System, Suikoden I&II HD Remaster official Asia-English website
coverage_rule: Every individually named character with a discrete prose character card in the selected official Suikoden I remaster page: Apple, Alen, Kasumi, Clive, Glenshiel, Stallion, Tai Ho, Teo, Tengaar, Valeria, Viki, Hix, Futch, Mathiu, Yam Koo, Lepant, and Luc (17 total). The card set—not all recruitable characters or every name in the prologue—is the bounded, reproducible witness. The player-addressed Hero is player-named/controlled and not a stable node. Uncarded names such as Barbarossa, Gremio, Cleo, Pahn, Ted, Black, Mathiu's teacher/student references, and Leknaat remain contextual omissions; runes, armies, organizations, ranks, species, places, Stars of Destiny, weapons, and mechanics are dimensions/terms rather than nodes.
omissions: The player-addressed Hero/protagonist, player-selected party/recruitment/order/equipment/formation/duel/war decisions, and all player-variable outcomes.

Every named figure absent from the selected page's card set, including Barbarossa, Gremio, Cleo, Pahn, Ted, Black, Mathiu and Leknaat where they occur only as contextual names, plus generic soldiers, armies, organizations, runes, weapons, dragon knights, dragons, factions, places, Stars of Destiny, and mechanics as nodes.

Suikoden II, its named protagonist and Jowy, the original 1995/1998 releases as independent editions, sequel/side-game/anime material, other localizations, remaster patch states, fan wikis, Wikipedia, walkthroughs, and community databases.
uncertainties: The official character page is a curated 17-card presentation, not a complete roster or in-game script; pass-complete applies only to that stated card set.

Konami says the collection aims to keep the original story and colorful cast intact while adding HD presentation and quality-of-life features. It is not evidence that every original release, localization, port, or later revision has identical wording or system behavior.
The story/prologue uses second person for the Hero and the system describes variable recruitment, party residence, and player choices; these are not universal named-character facts.
Only relationships explicitly stated between two characters that are both carded endpoints are retained. Contextual names do not become endpoint records by implication.
evidence_basis: Official Konami English remaster pages: character-level cards for all selected records, official system text for source-native mechanics, and an official dated launch announcement for version/release boundary. No fan resource is used as canonical evidence.
